cards.text: David, Israel's king, wrote this song for the choirmaster, back when he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab, commander of David's army (2 Samuel 8:16), came back and struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. Then David starts talking straight to God, and I'm leaning in like it's the last cookie on the tray.

cards.question: David opens his song talking straight to God. What does David say God has done to His people?

cards.text: Rejected, broken, angry. David does NOT tiptoe around God, he walks right in and puts it ALL on the counter, then finishes with one big ask: 'restore us!'

cards.question: David keeps going. He says God has shaken the land and torn it open. True or false?
David asks God to heal the land's fractures, because the land is ___.
Next, David tells God that His people have had nothing but easy days. True or false?

cards.text: David says God has shown His people hardship, and they're staggered from the wine He made them drink. I know staggering, friend: my first hop on this gold base after years in the back of a junk drawer, I wobbled around the bakery like the floor was MOVING.
Next, David says God has raised a banner for those who fear Him. After all that shaking and staggering, friend, that banner is the first thing in this whole song that goes UP.

cards.question: God has raised a banner for those who fear Him. What's it there for?

answers.text: So they can flee the bow
So they can mark the border
So they can count the troops

cards.text: Then David makes another big ask. He wants God to respond and save them with His right hand.

cards.question: David asks God to respond and save with His right hand, so that His ___ may be delivered.

cards.text: Now David brings in God's own words: God has spoken from His sanctuary. And when GOD speaks, friend, the whole bakery goes quiet, even the ovens.

cards.question: David has been praying about rejection and hardship. Then come God's words from His sanctuary. How do they open?

cards.text: God says, 'I will triumph!' Then, like a ROLL CALL, He names parts of Israel one after another: Shechem, the Valley of Succoth, Gilead and Manasseh.

cards.question: In this roll call, God says Gilead is His and Manasseh is His. True or false?
God calls Ephraim His helmet and Judah His scepter. What do those two pictures have in common?

answers.text: Things God is still looking for

cards.text: Then God turns to the nations nearby. Moab is His washbasin, and upon Edom He tosses His sandal, and friend, out of everybody on that list, I would NOT want to be the one catching the SANDAL.

cards.question: Over Philistia, God says He'll weep in sorrow. True or false?

cards.text: Over Philistia, God shouts in triumph. That's the end of God's words, and now David's back with a question of his own.

cards.question: David asks, 'Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to ___?'

cards.text: Then David asks, 'Have You not rejected us, O God?' There's that word again, rejected, back like an oven timer I SWEAR I already turned off.

cards.question: In that same breath, David asks if God will no longer do something with their armies. What is it?

cards.text: Next, David asks God for aid against the enemy. And he doesn't leave anybody guessing why it has to come from God, he says it right out loud.

cards.question: David asks God for aid against the enemy, because the help of ___ is worthless.
In the last line of the song, David says God will trample their enemies. True or false?

cards.text: And there it is: 'With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies.' The fight's still out there, but David knows who he's going in with, and friend, that changes EVERYTHING.
